# CRUD Requirements Checklist: Monitoring Configuration

**Purpose**: Review completeness, clarity, consistency, and testability of the Monitoring Configuration CRUD requirements.
**Created**: 2026-09-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are all persisted identity and lifecycle fields, including which values are optional, specified consistently? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the listing's displayed fields, actions, loading/empty/error states, search behavior, and navigation destinations all defined? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002–FR-005]
- [ ] CHK003 Are create inputs, disabled-by-default status, and the later explicit enablement action unambiguously covered across the create flow? [Completeness, Spec §US1 AC1, AC7; FR-006]
- [ ] CHK004 Are details and edit requirements explicit about editable fields and preserved identifier/creation date? [Completeness, Spec §US2 AC1–AC3; FR-012–FR-014]
- [ ] CHK005 Are successful, canceled, and failed deletion outcomes distinguished, including what remains available for future history? [Completeness, Spec §US3 AC1–AC5; FR-017–FR-018]
- [ ] CHK006 Are user-facing feedback requirements covered for validation, unavailable records, API failures, lifecycle actions, and recovery guidance? [Coverage, Spec §FR-019]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Are trimming, blank-name rejection, optional-description normalization, and URL validation rules precise enough to produce the same result at every boundary? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007–FR-010]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the accepted GitLab URL shape clear about absolute HTTP(S) URLs with a host, including any intended handling of ports, paths, query strings, fragments, and user information? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK009 Is the meaning of an “active” configuration distinct from enabled/disabled status and retired status wherever those terms are used? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, FR-012–FR-018]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the expected user-visible behavior after a stale edit conflict clear, including how reload and reapply preserve the user's unsaved input? [Clarity, Spec §US2 AC7; FR-014]
- [ ] CHK011 Is the optional idempotency key's purpose and format clear and distinct from the backend-generated configuration ID, including behavior when absent, invalid, or reused? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020–FR-021]
- [ ] CHK012 Is logical deletion clearly distinguished from physical erasure so the user-facing promise and future history-retention purpose do not conflict? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017–FR-018]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK013 Are the create form/API prohibition on setting enabled status and the update/lifecycle ability to enable later consistent across the user stories, requirements, and assumptions? [Consistency, Spec §US1 AC1/AC7; FR-006, FR-013, FR-015]
- [ ] CHK014 Are no-op status changes consistently specified not to create side effects or advance the update date, while actual changes do? [Consistency, Spec §US2 AC4–AC5; FR-015–FR-016]
- [ ] CHK015 Are the search normalization and matching rules consistent between the listing acceptance scenario, edge cases, and assumptions? [Consistency, Spec §US1 AC4; FR-004; Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK016 Are retired/unknown record outcomes consistent across details, edit, deletion, and ordinary listing requirements? [Consistency, Spec §US2 AC6; US3 AC3–AC5; FR-018]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK017 Can each success criterion be objectively assessed from defined persisted outcomes, user feedback, or contract behavior without relying on subjective judgments? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK018 Does SC-010 make clear that creation itself never enables a configuration and that only a later explicit successful action changes availability? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-010]
- [ ] CHK019 Are the criteria for advancing `updated_at` precise for actual changes, no-op requests, validation rejection, and failed persistence? [Measurability, Spec §FR-014–FR-016; SC-003]

## Scenario and Edge-Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK020 Are create retries, same-key/different-payload conflicts, and distinct creation intents with identical values fully distinguished? [Coverage, Spec §US1 AC6; FR-021; Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK021 Are concurrent edits and a record becoming unavailable during edit or delete covered with defined non-destructive outcomes? [Coverage, Spec §US2 AC6–AC7; US3 AC5; Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 Are duplicate names explicitly supported without ambiguity in finding, opening, and editing the intended configuration? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-007; Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK023 Are empty search, no matches, literal special characters, and whitespace-only search outcomes specified consistently? [Coverage, Spec §FR-004; Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements and Scope

- [ ] CHK024 Are API validation, conflict, unavailable-resource, and unexpected-error outcomes specified clearly enough for independent frontend/backend contract evolution? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019–FR-020]
- [ ] CHK025 Are data-retention requirements sufficient to preserve future execution context after configuration edits or retirement, without implying execution-history implementation in this feature? [Dependency, Spec §FR-014, FR-018, FR-025]
- [ ] CHK026 Are security boundaries for credentials and authentication explicit, including the fact that neither is accepted or implied in this feature? [Scope, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK027 Are accessibility, responsive behavior, and user-facing state requirements for these CRUD workflows explicitly specified or intentionally delegated to Feature 001's established patterns? [Gap, Spec §FR-003, FR-019, FR-023; Constitution §XI]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK028 Is the single-user/no-ownership assumption documented as a deliberate boundary, with no unspecified cross-user visibility or access-control behavior? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the expected initial collection size or a threshold for revisiting pagination documented consistently with the plan's no-pagination decision? [Dependency, Spec §FR-002, FR-004; Plan §Scale/Scope]
- [ ] CHK030 Are dependencies on Feature 001's shell, routes, shared components, and terminology sufficiently bounded to prevent this feature from silently changing the established application shell? [Dependency, Spec §FR-023–FR-024]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add reviewer comments or findings inline and link relevant resources where useful.
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference.
